column1: Luma.Green — Platform Design Analysis & Product Strategy

column2: Material chain stops too early at 'recycler'.
column3: Create explicit user types for pre-processor, washer, granulator, stripper, shredder, compounder, recovery processor and manufacturer.
column4: Manufacturers buy specific intermediate grades, not generic 'waste'.
column5: User, facility, process, material grade, lot

column2: One physical material changes identity after every process.
column3: Create a Material State graph: discarded → sorted → baled → processed → washed → flaked → pelletised → compounded → finished product.
column4: Makes circular value visible and traceable.

column3: Separate Main Product, Saleable By-product, Recoverable Waste and Residual Waste.
column4: Allows secondary streams to become new listings and revenue.

column3: Quote by grade + specification + geography + quantity, not only by broad material name.
column4: Reduces price mismatch and failed trades.
column5: Material code, grade, QC, price, quantity

column2: Small yards lack reliable B2B demand.
column3: Buyer request board + standing purchase orders + recurring demand.
column4: Improves yard working capital and reduces inventory days.
column5: Buyer profile, demand lot, preferred specs

column3: Supplier qualification + samples + QC records + acceptance history.
column4: Moves platform from scrap marketplace to industrial feedstock marketplace.

column3: Onboarding should verify registrations/consents relevant to the material and process; show expiry and status.

column2: Traceability is weak across multiple hand-offs.
column3: Every hand-off creates immutable transaction event with weight, price, timestamp, origin and destination.
column4: Supports audit, EPR and dispute resolution.

column3: Route optimisation and load consolidation by material/grade/route.
column4: A low-value material can become uneconomic after freight.

column3: Digital QC checklist, photo evidence, sample upload and buyer acceptance status.
column4: Turns 'trust' into a workflow rather than a rating alone.

column2: Residual waste still needs a route.
column3: Residual-routing engine should prohibit ordinary marketplace sale where controlled handling is required.
column4: Protects the platform from uncontrolled movement of regulated waste.

column2: Data is fragmented by material family.
column3: Create a common taxonomy with family → grade → state → process → output.
column4: Allows search across sectors and transformation chains.

column3: Build mass-balance ledger: input weight → recovered products + by-products + residuals.
column4: Creates verified impact metrics and chain-of-custody data.

column2: The platform should not merely 'sell waste'.
column3: Position Luma.Green as a circular industrial material exchange with traceable transformation.
column4: Creates a B2B value proposition beyond pickup.
column5: Marketplace, material graph, buyer demand, traceability

column1: Recommended core architecture: Marketplace + Material Graph + Lot Ledger + QC Layer + Compliance Layer + Logistics + EPR/Impact.
